reference_review.scope: The fixture's acceptance bands for five refuters on a confounded linear model with true ATE 2. The retained generator draws a seeded n=400 sample of that model, runs the public DoWhy 0.14 refuters and checks that DoWhy's own results satisfy the bands (placebo, dummy-outcome, random-common-cause, data-subset shifts and bootstrap proximity).
reference_review.independence_basis: The script uses only public DoWhy APIs on a repository-authored seeded simulation and imports no Antecedent code. It checks the bands against an independent implementation; it does not feed the product's own deterministic test data to DoWhy and does not compare product outputs to DoWhy outputs, so the bands remain product-chosen acceptance thresholds whose DoWhy-consistency is supported on one comparable model. The product refuters are tested on a deterministic non-random dataset in the Rust unit tests.
reference_review.historical_exposure: Original harness deleted (preserved in historical_oracle); the original DoWhy outputs were never recorded in the fixture, so what the bands were calibrated against cannot be reconstructed. The replacement was written from the public DoWhy method names; no DoWhy source or tests were consulted.
reference_review.redistribution: Repository-authored MIT OR Apache-2.0 script. DoWhy (MIT) and its dependencies are isolated locked tooling outside the product and ordinary CI; no upstream source or tests are stored.
reference_review.limitations: One simulated model and seed; DoWhy results are Monte Carlo and checked only against the bands, not at a numerical tolerance. The unobserved-common-cause band is not verified here because DoWhy parameterizes confounder strength differently from the product's residual-SD units. The bands establish that refuters do not falsify a correct linear adjustment, not that they detect violations (power) or that refuter p-values are calibrated. Calibration remains deferred.
